title: str — Text Sequence Type
description: Textual data in Python is handled with str objects, or strings. Strings are immutable sequences of Unicode code points. String literals are written in a variety of ways.
note: Strings are immutable sequences. This means that once created, you cannot change them. Operations that appear to modify a string actually create a new string.

methods.name: str.capitalize
methods.description: Return a copy of the string with its first character capitalized and the rest lowercased.

methods.name: str.casefold
methods.description: Return a casefolded copy of the string. Casefolded strings may be used for caseless matching.

methods.name: str.center
methods.description: Return centered in a string of length width. Padding is done using the specified fillchar (default is an ASCII space).

methods.name: str.count
methods.description: Return the number of non-overlapping occurrences of substring sub in the range [start, end].

methods.name: str.encode
methods.description: Return the string encoded to bytes.

methods.name: str.endswith
methods.description: Return True if the string ends with the specified suffix, otherwise return False. suffix can also be a tuple of suffixes to look for.

methods.name: str.expandtabs
methods.description: Return a copy of the string where all tab characters are replaced by one or more spaces.

methods.name: str.find
methods.description: Return the lowest index in the string where substring sub is found within the slice s[start:end]. Return -1 if sub is not found.
methods.note: The find() method should be used only if you need to know the position of sub. To check if sub is a substring or not, use the in operator.

methods.name: str.format
methods.description: Perform a string formatting operation. The string on which this method is called can contain literal text or replacement fields delimited by braces {}.

methods.name: str.format_map
methods.description: Similar to str.format(**mapping), except that mapping is used directly and not copied to a dict.

methods.name: str.index
methods.description: Like find(), but raise ValueError when the substring is not found.

methods.name: str.isalnum
methods.description: Return True if all characters in the string are alphanumeric and there is at least one character, False otherwise.

methods.name: str.isalpha
methods.description: Return True if all characters in the string are alphabetic and there is at least one character, False otherwise.

methods.name: str.isascii
methods.description: Return True if the string is empty or all characters in the string are ASCII, False otherwise.

methods.name: str.isdecimal
methods.description: Return True if all characters in the string are decimal characters and there is at least one character, False otherwise.

methods.name: str.isdigit
methods.description: Return True if all characters in the string are digits and there is at least one character, False otherwise.

methods.name: str.isidentifier
methods.description: Return True if the string is a valid Python identifier according to the language definition.

methods.name: str.islower
methods.description: Return True if all cased characters in the string are lowercase and there is at least one cased character, False otherwise.

methods.name: str.isnumeric
methods.description: Return True if all characters in the string are numeric characters, and there is at least one character, False otherwise.

methods.name: str.isprintable
methods.description: Return True if all characters in the string are printable or the string is empty, False otherwise.

methods.name: str.isspace
methods.description: Return True if there are only whitespace characters in the string and there is at least one character, False otherwise.

methods.name: str.istitle
methods.description: Return True if the string is a titlecased string and there is at least one character.

methods.name: str.isupper
methods.description: Return True if all cased characters in the string are uppercase and there is at least one cased character, False otherwise.

methods.name: str.join
methods.description: Return a string which is the concatenation of the strings in iterable. A TypeError will be raised if there are any non-string values in iterable.

methods.name: str.ljust
methods.description: Return the string left justified in a string of length width. Padding is done using the specified fillchar (default is an ASCII space).

methods.name: str.lower
methods.description: Return a copy of the string with all the cased characters converted to lowercase.

methods.name: str.lstrip
methods.description: Return a copy of the string with leading characters removed. The chars argument is a string specifying the set of characters to be removed.

methods.name: str.maketrans
methods.description: This static method returns a translation table usable for str.translate().

methods.name: str.partition
methods.description: Split the string at the first occurrence of sep, and return a 3-tuple containing the part before the separator, the separator itself, and the part after the separator.

methods.name: str.removeprefix
methods.description: If the string starts with the prefix string, return string[len(prefix):]. Otherwise, return a copy of the original string.

methods.name: str.removesuffix
methods.description: If the string ends with the suffix string and that suffix is not empty, return string[:-len(suffix)]. Otherwise, return a copy of the original string.

methods.name: str.replace
methods.description: Return a copy of the string with all occurrences of substring old replaced by new. If the optional argument count is given, only the first count occurrences are replaced.

methods.name: str.rfind
methods.description: Return the highest index in the string where substring sub is found, such that sub is contained within s[start:end]. Return -1 on failure.

methods.name: str.rindex
methods.description: Like rfind() but raises ValueError when the substring sub is not found.

methods.name: str.rjust
methods.description: Return the string right justified in a string of length width. Padding is done using the specified fillchar (default is an ASCII space).

methods.name: str.rpartition
methods.description: Split the string at the last occurrence of sep, and return a 3-tuple containing the part before the separator, the separator itself, and the part after the separator.

methods.name: str.rsplit
methods.description: Return a list of the words in the string, using sep as the delimiter string. If maxsplit is given, at most maxsplit splits are done, the rightmost ones.

methods.name: str.rstrip
methods.description: Return a copy of the string with trailing characters removed. The chars argument is a string specifying the set of characters to be removed.

methods.name: str.split
methods.description: Return a list of the words in the string, using sep as the delimiter string. If maxsplit is given, at most maxsplit splits are done (thus, the list will have at most maxsplit+1 elements).

methods.name: str.splitlines
methods.description: Return a list of the lines in the string, breaking at line boundaries. Line breaks are not included in the resulting list unless keepends is given and true.

methods.name: str.startswith
methods.description: Return True if string starts with the prefix, otherwise return False. prefix can also be a tuple of prefixes to look for.

methods.name: str.strip
methods.description: Return a copy of the string with the leading and trailing characters removed. The chars argument is a string specifying the set of characters to be removed.

methods.name: str.swapcase
methods.description: Return a copy of the string with uppercase characters converted to lowercase and vice versa.

methods.name: str.title
methods.description: Return a titlecased version of the string where words start with an uppercase character and the remaining characters are lowercase.

methods.name: str.translate
methods.description: Return a copy of the string in which each character has been mapped through the given translation table.

methods.name: str.upper
methods.description: Return a copy of the string with all the cased characters converted to uppercase.

methods.name: str.zfill
methods.description: Return a copy of the string left filled with ASCII '0' digits to make a string of length width. A leading sign prefix ('+'/'-') is handled by inserting the padding after the sign character rather than before.

printf_style_formatting.description: String objects have one unique built-in operation: the % operator (modulo). This is also known as the string formatting or interpolation operator.

conversion_specifiers.description: String (converts any Python object using str())
String (converts any Python object using repr())
Floating point format. Uses lowercase exponential format if exponent is less than -4 or not less than precision, decimal format otherwise
Floating point format. Uses uppercase exponential format if exponent is less than -4 or not less than precision, decimal format otherwise
No argument is converted, results in a '%' character in the result

format_specification_mini_language.description: The str.format() method and the Formatter class share the same syntax for format strings (although in the case of Formatter, subclasses can define their own format string syntax).

align_options.description: Forces the field to be left-aligned within the available space (this is the default for most objects)
Forces the field to be right-aligned within the available space (this is the default for numbers)
Forces the padding to be placed after the sign (if any) but before the digits
Forces the field to be centered within the available space

sign_options.description: Indicates that a sign should be used for both positive as well as negative numbers
Indicates that a sign should be used only for negative numbers (this is the default behavior)
Indicates that a leading space should be used on positive numbers, and a minus sign on negative numbers

type_options.description: String format. This is the default type for strings and may be omitted
Binary format. Outputs the number in base 2
Character. Converts the integer to the corresponding unicode character before printing
Decimal Integer. Outputs the number in base 10
Octal format. Outputs the number in base 8
Hex format. Outputs the number in base 16, using lower-case letters for the digits above 9
Hex format. Outputs the number in base 16, using upper-case letters for the digits above 9
Number. This is the same as 'd', except that it uses the current locale setting to insert the appropriate number separator characters
Exponent notation. Prints the number in scientific notation using the letter 'e' to indicate the exponent
Exponent notation. Same as 'e' except it uses an upper case 'E' as the separator character
Fixed-point notation. Displays the number as a fixed-point number
Fixed-point notation. Same as 'f', but converts nan to NAN and inf to INF
General format. For a given precision p >= 1, this rounds the number to p significant digits
General format. Same as 'g' except switches to 'E' if the number gets too large
Percentage. Multiplies the number by 100 and displays in fixed ('f') format, followed by a percent sign

formatted_string_literals.description: Formatted string literals (also called f-strings for short) let you include the value of Python expressions inside a string by prefixing the string with f or F and writing expressions as {expression}.

examples.code:
>>> name = 'Fred'
>>> f'He said his name is {name}.'
"He said his name is Fred."
